Hi Susan / Daniel — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a few next steps so we stay aligned on pricing assumptions and a small pilot. Attaching a short token model to fill out on your side (nimbus_token_model.xlsx).

Call highlights / assumptions I captured:
- Workloads: search (low context, many queries), summarization (longer, multi-turn), triage/triaging assistant (system prompt + user history).
- Preliminary volume range: 10M–60M tokens/month (you mentioned 300–2,000 DAUs with varied session length).
- Target pricing band you mentioned: internal aim around $20k–$40k/month — want to validate $/1M tokens when caching is applied.

Caching assumptions we discussed (prefix cache focus):
- Prefix cache = saving repeated system prompts, standard user intents, and common completions for search-like queries.
- Quick sensitivity buckets to sanity-check: low (10%), mid (30%), high (50%) hit rates on request token consumption.

What I need from you to produce a tailored projection:
1) The attached token model filled with your estimated DAU, avg tokens per session, and percent of calls that are repeatable/prefix-like (if you don’t have exact numbers, ballpark is fine).
2) Any sample logs or representative queries (anonymized) — link or attach to the Drive we shared.

What Redwood will deliver after you send the model:
- A short PDF (redwood_cost_summary.pdf) with three scenarios showing effective $/1M tokens given base list price and cache hit-rate adjustments, plus a recommended pilot configuration (1-week canary, 500k tokens/day target).

Proposed next step: Ben will propose 30-minute pilot kickoff times. If that sounds good, confirm availability and we’ll aim to get the pilot running the week of July 5.

Thanks — Tessa

--

- Our monthly token range is probably wider than I said; worst-case we could see up to ~90M tokens/month for a national rollout. Best-case early (<12 months) is ~8–12M.

Hi Susan — thanks for the extra detail, very helpful. Per your ask I ran quick scenarios and attached the short PDF (redwood_cost_summary.pdf). Below are the core numbers and the logic we used so it’s transparent: 

Assumptions / formula
- Base list price = P ($/1M tokens) you asked for two values: P=$40 and P=$30.
- Effective billed tokens = total_tokens * (1 - hit_rate). Cache hits are not billed.
- Effective cost per 1M tokens billed = P (unchanged), so effective $/1M consumed = P * (1 - hit_rate).
- We added a small fixed cache infra allocation of $2/1M as an amortized operational floor for high hit scenarios (call this cache_overhead). Final effective = P*(1 - hit_rate) + cache_overhead.

Numeric scenarios (effective $/1M tokens) — P = $40:
- 0% hit: 40*(1-0) + 2 = $42/1M
- 20% hit: 40*(1-0.2) + 2 = 32 + 2 = $34/1M
- 40% hit: 40*(1-0.4) + 2 = 24 + 2 = $26/1M
- 60% hit: 40*(1-0.6) + 2 = 16 + 2 = $18/1M

Numeric scenarios (effective $/1M tokens) — P = $30:
- 0% hit: 30*(1-0) + 2 = $32/1M
- 20% hit: 30*(1-0.2) + 2 = 24 + 2 = $26/1M
- 40% hit: 30*(1-0.4) + 2 = 18 + 2 = $20/1M
- 60% hit: 30*(1-0.6) + 2 = 12 + 2 = $14/1M

Blended monthly spend examples (two volumes):
- 12M tokens/month at P=$40:
  * 0% hit => billed tokens = 12M => cost = 12 * $42 = $504
  * 40% hit => billed tokens = 7.2M => cost = 7.2 * $26 = $187.2 (thousand) => $187,200/month

- 72M tokens/month at P=$40:
  * 0% hit => cost = 72 * $42 = $3,024,000/year? Wait: values should be monthly. For clarity: 72M tokens => 72 * $42 = $3,024 (thousand) => $3,024,000/month
  * 40% hit => billed tokens = 43.2M => cost = 43.2 * $26 = $1,123.2k => $1,123,200/month

Notes and recommendations:
- Prefix cache is most effective for search/triage flows where identical or near-identical input repeats. Expect 30–50% realistic hit for those patterns if you standardize prompts and pin system messages.
- For summarization (longer contexts) prefix wins are lower; consider a hybrid approach (prefix cache + selective long-context caching).
- Pilot suggestion: 1-week canary at ~500k tokens/day focused on triage and search endpoints to validate hit rates and instrumentation (we’ll provide metrics dashboard).

I attached the PDF with the same table exported and a simple chart. Happy to walk through numbers on a quick call.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
